message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"1.13","text":"While I was saying these things and what followed from them, a great uproar arose among the crowds. Some, as though pitying Barnabas, took my side, but others, being foolish, fiercely gnashed their teeth at me. When evening had at last overtaken us, I took Barnabas by the hand and, though he was unwilling, forcibly led him to my house. There I made him stay, so that no one might lay hands on him. After remaining for a few days and instructing me in a few matters concerning the true word—only a little, as was possible in a few days—he said that he was hastening to Judaea for the sake of the religious festival, since he wished from then on to be with his own compatriots.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"συνήραντό μοι","chosen":"took my side","rationale":"The phrase describes joining Clement in support of Barnabas."},{"source_quote":"δεινῶς κατ’ ἐμοῦ ἔβρυχον τοὺς ὀδόντας","chosen":"fiercely gnashed their teeth at me","rationale":"Preserves both the hostile image and its direction against Clement."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ ἀληθοῦς λόγου","chosen":"concerning the true word","rationale":"Retains λόγος as “word” without substituting a later theological formula."},{"source_quote":"ὀλίγον ὡς ἐν ὀλίγαις ἡμέραις","chosen":"only a little, as was possible in a few days","rationale":"The compressed parenthesis qualifies how little instruction the short stay allowed."},{"source_quote":"τῆς κατὰ τὴν θρησκείαν ἑορτῆς","chosen":"the religious festival","rationale":"The source associates the festival with religious observance but does not identify it more specifically."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς ἑαυτοῦ ὁμοεθνέσιν","chosen":"with his own compatriots","rationale":"The term denotes people belonging to the same nation or ethnic community."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"1.14","text":"But I could plainly see that he had grown weary. For when I said, “Only set out for me the words of the man who appeared, the words you heard, and I will embellish them with discourse of my own and proclaim God’s will. Then, in this way, within a few days I will sail with you—for I greatly long to be in the regions of Judaea—and perhaps I will even live with you for the whole course of my life,” he heard this and replied, “If you want to investigate our affairs and learn what is beneficial, sail with me immediately. Otherwise, at least, today I will tell you the directions to my dwelling and what you want to know, so that whenever you wish, you may come and present yourself to us; for tomorrow I will depart for my own place.” Then, seeing that he could not be persuaded, I went with him as far as the harbor. After learning from him the directions to the dwelling places that he had mentioned, I said to him, “Were it not that tomorrow I am collecting something owed to me, I would sail with you immediately. Nevertheless, I will catch up with you very soon.” After saying this and entrusting him to those in charge of the ship, I turned back grieving, remembering my good and intimate friend.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἀποναρκήσας","chosen":"had grown weary","rationale":"The verb suggests becoming numb, listless, or disinclined; the context concerns Barnabas’s reaction to further delay."},{"source_quote":"τοὺς τοῦ φανέντος ἀνδρὸς οὓς ἤκουσας ἐκτίθου λόγους","chosen":"set out for me the words of the man who appeared, the words you heard","rationale":"Preserves both the attribution of the words and the relative clause identifying them as words Barnabas heard."},{"source_quote":"τῷ ἐμῷ κοσμήσας λόγῳ","chosen":"embellish them with discourse of my own","rationale":"κοσμέω describes Clement’s proposed rhetorical adornment of the reported words."},{"source_quote":"ἱστορῆσαι τὰ ἡμέτερα","chosen":"to investigate our affairs","rationale":"ἱστορέω denotes learning through inquiry rather than necessarily composing a history."},{"source_quote":"ἐξ αὐτῆς","chosen":"immediately","rationale":"The elliptical idiom indicates acting from that very moment."},{"source_quote":"ἐπεί γε τὰ σημεῖα τῆς οἰκήσεώς μου καὶ ὧν θέλεις ἐγώ σοι σήμερον ἐρῶ","chosen":"Otherwise, at least, today I will tell you the directions to my dwelling and what you want to know","rationale":"In this response ἐπεί γε introduces the alternative if Clement does not sail at once; the coordination with ὧν θέλεις is compressed."},{"source_quote":"ἐπιστῇς ἡμῖν","chosen":"you may come and present yourself to us","rationale":"The verb denotes coming to and standing before or joining Barnabas and his associates."},{"source_quote":"ἀδυσώπητον","chosen":"he could not be persuaded","rationale":"The adjective describes someone unmoved by entreaty or pressure."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ τὰ ἐμαυτοῦ","chosen":"for my own place","rationale":"The substantival expression may refer to Barnabas’s home, people, or affairs; the rendering preserves that ellipsis."},{"source_quote":"τῶν οἰκήσεων","chosen":"the dwelling places","rationale":"The plural is retained, although Barnabas previously referred to his dwelling in the singular."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"1.15","text":"After spending some days there and being unable to receive the debt in full, for the sake of speed I disregarded the remainder as an impediment and myself sailed away to Judaea. In fifteen days I reached Caesarea of Strato. Once I had set foot on land and was seeking lodging, I learned that a certain man named Peter, the most highly regarded disciple of the man who had appeared in Judaea and had performed signs and wonders, was to hold a verbal debate the next day with Simon the Samaritan from Gittha. When I heard this, I asked that his lodging be pointed out to me; and in like manner I learned it and stood at the gateway. When those in the house saw me, they questioned me about who I was and where I had come from. And behold, Barnabas came out and, as soon as he saw me, embraced me, rejoicing greatly and weeping. Taking me by the hand, he led me in to where Peter was and said to me, “This is Peter, whom I announced to you as greatest in the wisdom of God. I spoke to him about you without ceasing, as you will find out for yourself, because I truthfully set before him all the good things concerning you. At the same time I also disclosed your intention, with the result that he himself longs to see you too. Therefore, through my own hands, I present you to him as a great gift.” After saying this and presenting me, he said, “This is Clement, Peter.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τὸ χρέος οὐχ. ὅλον λαβεῖν δυνηθείς","chosen":"being unable to receive the debt in full","rationale":"The translation construes οὐχ with ὅλον despite the intervening printed full stop."},{"source_quote":"δεκαπέντε ἡμερῶν εἰς Καισάρειαν κατήντησα τὴν Στράτωνος","chosen":"In fifteen days I reached Caesarea of Strato","rationale":"The genitive expresses the period occupied by the journey, and Στράτωνος distinguishes this Caesarea."},{"source_quote":"ζήτησιν ποιεῖται λόγων","chosen":"was to hold a verbal debate","rationale":"The expression denotes a formal inquiry or dispute conducted through speech."},{"source_quote":"καὶ ὁμῶς ἔμαθον","chosen":"and in like manner I learned it","rationale":"The rendering follows the printed adverb ὁμῶς rather than silently changing it to ὅμως, though its precise discourse force here is uncertain."},{"source_quote":"ἀντέβαλλον τίς τε ὢν καὶ πόθεν ἥκω","chosen":"they questioned me about who I was and where I had come from","rationale":"In this setting ἀντιβάλλω introduces questions concerning Clement’s identity and origin."},{"source_quote":"ὃν μέγιστον ἐπὶ τῇ τοῦ θεοῦ σοφίᾳ ἐπηγγελλόμην σοι","chosen":"whom I announced to you as greatest in the wisdom of God","rationale":"The construction recalls Barnabas’s earlier commendation of Peter while retaining the qualification concerning God’s wisdom."},{"source_quote":"ᾧ ἀπαύστως σε ἀντέβαλλον","chosen":"I spoke to him about you without ceasing","rationale":"The verb here denotes repeatedly bringing Clement before Peter in conversation or report."},{"source_quote":"ὡς εἴσει ἐκ ταὐτομάτου","chosen":"as you will find out for yourself","rationale":"The idiom indicates that Clement will come to know the truth directly or of his own accord."},{"source_quote":"ὅτι πάντα τὰ κατὰ σὲ καλὰ ὄντα ἀψευδῶς ἀντέβαλλον","chosen":"because I truthfully set before him all the good things concerning you","rationale":"The rendering preserves ὅτι as causal and explicitly represents ἀψευδῶς as describing the report’s truthfulness."},{"source_quote":"ἅμα καὶ τὴν προαίρεσιν ἐξέφανα","chosen":"At the same time I also disclosed your intention","rationale":"προαίρεσις denotes Clement’s purpose or settled disposition, while ἐκφαίνω makes it known."},{"source_quote":"ὡς αὐτὸν γλίχεσθαι καὶ ἰδεῖν σε","chosen":"with the result that he himself longs to see you too","rationale":"The construction is taken as consecutive, with αὐτόν as the subject of the infinitives and σε as the object of ἰδεῖν."},{"source_quote":"καὶ τοῦτ᾿ εἰπὼν προσενέγκάς ἔφη","chosen":"After saying this and presenting me, he said","rationale":"The aorist participles describe Barnabas’s actions before his direct introduction of Clement."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τὸ χρέος οὐχ. ὅλον λαβεῖν δυνηθείς","issue":"The supplied print places a full stop after οὐχ, interrupting the phrase naturally read as οὐχ ὅλον. This is treated as a printed punctuation feature rather than a transcription error.","proposed_reading":"τὸ χρέος οὐχ ὅλον λαβεῖν δυνηθείς","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"τοῦ ἐν Ἰουδαίᾳ εἰσφανέντος ἀνδρὸς τοῦ σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα· πεποιηκότος ὁ δοκιμώτατος ὑπάρχων μαθητής","issue":"The printed high point after τέρατα separates the object phrase from πεποιηκότος. The participle most naturally modifies ἀνδρός and governs σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα, so the translation reads the construction continuously while retaining the supplied wording.","proposed_reading":"τοῦ ἐν Ἰουδαίᾳ εἰσφανέντος ἀνδρὸς τοῦ σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα πεποιηκότος, ὁ δοκιμώτατος ὑπάρχων μαθητής","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"καὶ ὁμῶς ἔμαθον","issue":"The printed ὁμῶς is a possible Greek adverb meaning “likewise” or “equally,” but its force in this context is uncertain. It has not been silently normalized to the more familiar ὅμως.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"1.16","text":"Good Peter sprang forward as soon as he heard the name and kissed me warmly. After making me sit down, he immediately said, “You did well when you magnanimously welcomed Barnabas, the herald of truth, in honor of the God who truly is, neither being ashamed nor fearing the anger of the uneducated crowds. You will be blessed. For just as you welcomed the ambassador of truth with every honor, so Truth herself will make you, though a stranger to her own city, a citizen of it. Then you will rejoice greatly because you have now lent a short-lived kindness—by which he meant a disposition toward good words. You will be an heir to eternal and inalienable good things. Do not tire yourself setting your character before me, for truthful Barnabas has set before us everything concerning you, making favorable mention of you nearly every day. And, to tell you briefly, as a genuine friend, the matter at hand: if nothing hinders you, travel with us, partaking of the discourses of truth that I intend to deliver from city to city, as far as Rome itself. And as for you, if there is anything you want, say it.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"κατεφίλησεν","chosen":"kissed me warmly","rationale":"The compound verb conveys an affectionate or emphatic kiss."},{"source_quote":"μεγαλοφρόνως","chosen":"magnanimously","rationale":"The adverb characterizes Clement’s reception of Barnabas as noble and high-minded."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ ὄντως θεοῦ","chosen":"the God who truly is","rationale":"Preserves the existential force of ὄντως rather than reducing the phrase to a conventional title."},{"source_quote":"αὐτή σε ἡ ἀλήθεια","chosen":"Truth herself","rationale":"Retains the emphatic personification of ἀλήθεια."},{"source_quote":"ξένον ὄντα τῆς ἰδίας πόλεως καταστήσει πολίτην","chosen":"will make you, though a stranger to her own city, a citizen of it","rationale":"Preserves the contrast between foreigner and citizen and the image of Truth possessing a city."},{"source_quote":"βραχεῖαν νῦν ἐδάνεισας χάριν","chosen":"you have now lent a short-lived kindness","rationale":"The rendering preserves the lending metaphor and takes βραχεῖαν temporally in contrast with the eternal goods that follow."},{"source_quote":"προαίρεσιν λόγων καλῶν λέγων","chosen":"by which he meant a disposition toward good words","rationale":"The parenthetical phrase appears to explain the preceding kindness, though its compressed syntax permits some uncertainty about the precise relation of λόγων καλῶν to προαίρεσιν."},{"source_quote":"ἀιδίων καὶ ἀναφαιρέτων ἀγαθῶν","chosen":"eternal and inalienable good things","rationale":"ἀναφαίρετος denotes what cannot be taken away, while the substantival plural ἀγαθῶν remains general."},{"source_quote":"μὴ κάμνε ἀντιβάλλειν μοι τὸ σὸν ἦθος","chosen":"Do not tire yourself setting your character before me","rationale":"Peter tells Clement not to labor at presenting or explaining his character, since Barnabas has already done so."},{"source_quote":"τὴν ἀγαθήν σου ποιούμενος μνήμην","chosen":"making favorable mention of you","rationale":"The idiom describes Barnabas’s repeated favorable remembrance or mention of Clement."},{"source_quote":"τὸ προκείμενον","chosen":"the matter at hand","rationale":"The expression refers to the proposal Peter is about to place before Clement."},{"source_quote":"μεταλαμβάνων τῶν τῆς ἀληθείας λόγων","chosen":"partaking of the discourses of truth","rationale":"The participle presents Clement as sharing in or receiving the discourses without making him their speaker."},{"source_quote":"ὧν κατὰ πόλιν ποιεῖσθαι μέλλω μέχρι Ῥώμης αὐτῆς","chosen":"that I intend to deliver from city to city, as far as Rome itself","rationale":"The relative refers to the discourses; ποιεῖσθαι λόγους means to give or conduct them, and κατὰ πόλιν distributes the activity across successive cities."},{"source_quote":"καὶ σὺ δὲ εἴ τι βούλει λέγε","chosen":"And as for you, if there is anything you want, say it","rationale":"The rendering preserves the shift back to Clement and Peter’s invitation for him to speak."}],"source_issues":[]}]}
